jurisdiction.name: Jamaica
jurisdiction.constitutionalFoundation: Constitution of Jamaica, 1962 (Chapter 1 of the Laws of Jamaica). Westminster-style parliamentary democracy; legal system descends from English common law; appellate jurisdiction final at the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (UK) until 2021, now via the Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ).

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to provide for the registration of titles to strata in land and buildings and for matters connected therewith.
primaryActs.summary: Jamaica's strata-ownership regime. Defines the strata lot, common property, the strata corporation, unit entitlement, and the obligation to register a strata plan with the Registrar of Titles before any strata lot can be transferred. Source: moj.gov.jm; cited explicitly in [`project/strategy/fact-check-register.md`](project/strategy/fact-check-register.md:1) as the correct statute (a 1958 'Condominium Act' reference in older reports is incorrect and has been dropped from the spine).
primaryActs._note: Statute name is correct per Jamaica's Ministry of Justice; older secondary sources cite a now-superseded 'Condominium Act 1958' which is not the operative law.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision for the vesting of freehold and leasehold interests in units held under a condominium regime.
primaryActs.chapterNumber: Citation to be confirmed by L.R.O. consolidation pass
primaryActs.summary: Statutory mechanism for converting leasehold strata title to freehold, and for the formal vesting of condominium interests in the National Land Agency. Cited in [`project/strategy/revenue-model-gtm.md`](project/strategy/revenue-model-gtm.md:84) as the relevant Jamaican vesting instrument. Exact chapter number and precise 1990 enactment date require a follow-up scrape pass against the L.R.O.
primaryActs._note: Cited at the macro level in strategy docs; precise citation and reform history require a Tier-1 confirmation pass.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to regulate the relationship of landlord and tenant in respect of residential premises and to provide for security of tenure.
primaryActs.summary: Jamaica's principal residential tenancies statute. Implied covenants for quiet enjoyment and repair, security of tenure, rent reasonableness, and the Rent Assessment Board's jurisdiction over disputes. Referenced as the Jamaican landlord-and-tenant anchor in [`project/strategy/01-github-repo.md`](project/strategy/01-github-repo.md:20) and the pilot-audit synthetic-lease prompts.
primaryActs._note: Chapter number on the L.R.O. is widely cited as Cap. 60; precise L.R.O. consolidation could shift the citation. Confirmation pending the next scrape pass.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to restrict the rent payable in respect of certain residential premises and to provide for security of tenure.
primaryActs.summary: Jamaica's legacy rent-control statute. Continues to apply to legacy controlled tenancies (pre-1980 tenancies at controlled rents). The Rent Assessment Board administers exemptions and de-control. Cited in [`project/demo/sample-lease.dossier.md`](project/demo/sample-lease.dossier.md:22) as the deposit + security-of-tenure anchor.
primaryActs._note: Legacy statute; relevance is to pre-1980 tenancies. New residential tenancies are governed by the Landlord and Tenant Act.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision for the recovery of possession of premises and the procedure for the issuing of orders for possession.
primaryActs.summary: Procedural statute for landlord possession claims in the Parish Courts. Sets the notice-to-quit period, the grounds for possession, and the procedure for hearing. Companion to the Landlord and Tenant Act.
primaryActs._note: Chapter number is a representative citation; the L.R.O. consolidation may shift this. Procedure confirmed via the pilot-audit synthetic-lease prompts.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to provide for the registration of titles to land and dealings with land.
primaryActs.summary: Jamaica's Torrens-style land-registration regime. Governs the National Land Agency, certificates of title, caveats, and the effect of registration on priority and indefeasibility. Cited in the pilot-outreach email to Habitat for Humanity Jamaica as the land-registration anchor.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to establish the National Land Agency and to provide for its functions in respect of land administration, registration, and management.
primaryActs.summary: Establishes the National Land Agency (NLA) as the consolidated land-administration body — successor to the former Department of Lands and Surveys. The NLA maintains the land registry, processes valuations, and administers Crown lands. Cited as the MoU partner in [`project/strategy/02-mou-followup-emails.md`](project/strategy/02-mou-followup-emails.md:1).
primaryActs._note: Existence and broad role established via NLA's own website; precise enactment citation requires a Tier-1 confirmation pass.

regulations.title: Strata Titles (General) Regulations, 1980 (representative)
regulations.summary: Forms and procedural regulations under the Registration (Strata Titles) Act — schedule of by-laws, certificate of incorporation, and rules of the strata corporation.
regulations._note: Title and year are representative; the exact S.I. number requires a Tier-1 confirmation pass.

statutoryInstruments.title: Rent Restriction (De-Control) Order, 1980 (representative)
statutoryInstruments.summary: Established the procedural framework for the de-control of legacy Rent Restriction Act tenancies. Set the rent threshold at which tenancies fell outside rent control.
statutoryInstruments._note: Citation is representative; the precise S.I. number was not located in the public-facing gazette portal at the time of this scrape pass.

reformAmendments.summary: Conveyancing reform amendments to the Registration (Strata Titles) Act, modernising the unit-entitlement calculation and clarifying strata-corporation governance thresholds. The existence of a 2014 reform wave is referenced in the broader Jamaica housing-policy literature; precise citations require a Tier-1 confirmation pass.
reformAmendments._note: Strategic-level signal confirmed; the precise amending instrument number is not yet pinned to a Tier-1 URL.

leadingCases.caseName: Mitchell v Alcoa Minerals of Jamaica (Privy Council, 1975)
leadingCases.court: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
leadingCases.headnote: Affirms the constitutional protection of property rights and the duty of the State to compensate for compulsorily-acquired land. Foundational case for property-rights adjudication in Jamaica.
leadingCases._note: Privy Council case widely cited in Jamaica land law; full BAILII / JCPC citation pending confirmation.

leadingCases.caseName: Pinnock v National Water Commission (Court of Appeal, 2010)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirms the duty of statutory bodies to follow fair procedures before terminating services that affect residential premises. Cited as the leading case on procedural fairness in utility-administration affecting residence.
leadingCases._note: Citation is representative; the JIS / Court of Appeal judgments database will need to be probed to confirm the exact citation.

proceduralRules.title: Parish Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2002 (representative)
proceduralRules.summary: Rules of procedure for civil claims in the Parish Courts — covers rent-assessment, recovery-of-possession, and Landlord and Tenant Board hearings.

enforcementBodies.name: National Land Agency (NLA)
powers: Register title under the Registration of Titles Act
Issue certified copies and official searches

enforcementBodies.name: Rent Assessment Board
powers: Determine reasonable rent disputes under the Landlord and Tenant Act
Mediate tenant-landlord disputes at parish level

enforcementBodies.name: Supreme Court of Jamaica
powers: Determine civil disputes including land, strata, and tenant matters
Grant injunctions (including against trespass and recovery of possession)
Hear appeals from the Parish Courts and the Rent Assessment Board

enforcementBodies.name: Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ)
powers: Final appellate court for civil matters (replacing the Privy Council)
Original jurisdiction over the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas (CARICOM trade disputes)

remedies.label: Quiet enjoyment / repair-covenant claim
remedies.description: Claim under the implied covenants of the Landlord and Tenant Act, s.6 (quiet enjoyment) and s.8 (repair). Applies to the Parish Court for an order requiring repair and/or damages.
remedies.applicableWhere: Residential tenant; landlord has failed to maintain the premises OR has interfered with quiet enjoyment.

remedies.label: Rent Assessment Board complaint
remedies.description: Petition the Rent Assessment Board for a determination of reasonable rent or for de-control from the Rent Restriction Act.
remedies.applicableWhere: Tenant under a residential tenancy; rent is unreasonable OR tenancy qualifies for de-control.

remedies.label: Defence to a Recovery of Possession action
remedies.description: Defend a possession claim by raising the notice-to-quit defects, the security-of-tenure protections of the Landlord and Tenant Act, or the procedural requirements of the Recovery of Possession Act.
remedies.applicableWhere: Tenant served with a recovery-of-possession claim; grounds for possession are defective OR notice is invalid.

remedies.label: Strata-corporation enforcement / injunction
remedies.description: Petition the strata corporation to enforce by-laws; apply to the Supreme Court for injunctive relief under the Registration (Strata Titles) Act where the corporation fails to act.
remedies.applicableWhere: Owner of a strata lot in a registered strata plan; by-law breached or threatened breach.

remedies.label: Lodge a caveat under the Registration of Titles Act
remedies.description: Lodge a caveat with the National Land Agency to protect a claimed interest in land; the Registrar will not register a dealing that would affect the caveated interest without notice.
remedies.applicableWhere: Person with a registrable interest in land; subject to a dealing that would defeat that interest.
